_comment: APPROVED BUILDS - which agent builds an identity accepts messages from.
THIS LIST ONLY GROWS. Every release adds its PROTECTION HASH here, and older machines pull the
file so they recognise builds published after they were installed. Without that, upgrading one
agent silently breaks its peers: they refuse it, and the refusal looks like an intermittent
network fault rather than a policy decision.
Entries are never deleted - a build that must no longer be trusted gets allow:false, so the
revocation itself propagates. Deleting a row would merely make older machines forget it was ever
a build, and they would keep accepting it.
Bump version whenever builds change; the tool reports it so an operator can see what they synced.

A protection hash is the SHA-512 of the extracted entry dll. It no longer requires a machine of that kind: the dll is embedded verbatim in the single-file bundle, so hashing the build's own intermediate dll gives the same value - verified on linux-x64 and confirmed on Apple Silicon for r14. See releases.json and ghreleasedocument.md.
